subject: Forensic log curation / retention window — follow-up from incident
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@acme.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Logs retention — request for forensics after 7/28 incident

Jonas,

Thanks again for the quick triage yesterday. Our security team needs to understand exactly how long Redwood will keep the raw request/response logs, edge load balancer traces, and any packet captures (if available) related to our tenant for the window around 2027-07-28 21:00 UTC. Specifically: 1) What is the default retention for those artifacts? 2) What are our options to preserve slices for a forensic handoff (and do you support secure transfer)? 3) Who is the internal point of contact for chain-of-custody paperwork?

We have a pending internal review and need an initial written preservation plan by Monday.

— Helen
Helen Park
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Acme Corp
helen.park@acme.com
+1 415 555 0142

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 10:03:07 -07:00
Subject: Re: Logs retention — request for forensics after 7/28 incident

Helen — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (security/forensics) and Evelyn (customer success) so we can provide a short preservation plan and next steps.

Quick answers up front:
- Default retention: API request/response logs (metadata only) = 30 days, detailed request bodies and embeddings = 14 days by default for hosted customers; application-layer tracing (edge LB traces) = 14 days.
- Preservation options: we can snapshot and escrow relevant artifacts for up to 90 days on request, or export a limited forensic slice (logs + KV cache snapshots) to a secure transfer link (S3 with customer-managed KMS) for handoff. For full packet captures we typically do not store PCAPs continuously, but we can perform a targeted capture if requested within 72 hours of the event and provide an archived copy subject to legal review.

We need to confirm the exact scope of artifacts Acme wants preserved and whether you require chain-of-custody documentation. Karthik — can you confirm the earliest we can generate a preservation bundle for the 7/28 window and any legal approvals? Evelyn — I propose we set up a 30-minute call with Acme to align on transfer method and sign the preservation request PDF.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference
Office: +1 650 555 0199

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:18:52 -07:00
Subject: Re: Logs retention — request for forensics after 7/28 incident

Jonas / Evelyn — internal note on feasibility and timeline:
- We can produce a preservation bundle containing: request/response logs (full payloads where available), server-side tracing (span IDs + timings), route-level access logs, and model inference metadata (model version, token counts, prompt hashes). This does not include customer PII unless it was in the payloads — we'll flag any such items.
- Timeline: If Acme signs the preservation request today, we can stage the export within 24 hours and deliver the archive within 48 hours.
- PCAPs: we do not retain PCAPs by default. We retain low-level network captures for 72 hours for troubleshooting on specific nodes; targeted capture must be requested immediately.
- Chain-of-custody: Security maintains a PDF handoff and checksum manifest; we can add a notarized signature on request but that requires legal sign-off.

I'll prepare a minimal preservation_request.pdf template that Evelyn can send to Acme to sign.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>

Subject: Preservation request & short plan (Acme Corp) — next steps

Helen — thanks for the patience. Attached is a one-page preservation_request.pdf that describes the artifacts we can provide, a suggested 90-day escrow window, and the secure transfer options (Redwood-hosted S3 with customer-managed KMS, or a signed rsync to your on-prem). If that looks good to you, please sign and return and we will begin staging.

Attachments:
- preservation_request.pdf (one-page preservation checklist and signature block)
- incident-20270729-session-metadata.csv (sample metadata slice)

Proposed quick plan:
1) Acme signs preservation_request.pdf (we can accept e-sign) — target: today
2) Redwood stages the bundle and shares secure link — target: within 48h after sign
3) Karthik provides chain-of-custody manifest; Evelyn coordinates transfer and post-handoff debrief — target: within 72h

If Acme needs a notarized chain, let us know and we'll escalate to legal.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.inference

Thanks — Evelyn, this looks acceptable. I attached a signed copy of the preservation_request.pdf (signed_preservation_acme.pdf). We want the full request/response payloads for the 21:00–21:30 UTC window and the corresponding span traces; PCAP not required if you can provide the trace spans. We also need an MD5 manifest for the bundle.

Can you confirm the transfer method and whether Redwood will rotate the customer-managed KMS key on the S3 bucket after transfer?

— Helen

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preservation request & short plan (Acme Corp) — transfer details and rotation

Helen — short update: we have staged a 7/28 21:00–21:30 UTC preservation bundle. Contents: full request/response payloads (where retained), span traces, route-level logs, and model metadata. Attachments below are a sample manifest and the stubbed PCAP note (we did not capture PCAPs beyond 72h).

Transfer method: secure S3 link encrypted with customer-managed KMS (we created an envelope KMS key that you control). Once you confirm receipt and checksum, Redwood will rotate the envelope key and revoke the temporary grant used for the transfer (standard process).

MD5 manifest: attached as incident-20270729-session-metadata.csv (contains checksums and file sizes). Please confirm you received the archive and that the manifest checksums match. After confirmation, Redwood will mark the bundle as delivered and the preservation flag will remain active for 90 days (unless you request earlier deletion).

If you want chain-of-custody notarization, loop in legal and we can escalate.

Thanks — Jonas
